Anna — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to provide a concise packet to import into your SIG. I'm looping in Kimberly (Security) and Diego (Infra) to provide the network diagram and KMS details.

High-level answers up-front: 
- Primary hosting: EU (Frankfurt) region only for this Private deployment/managed data plane. We will not write production request data to non-EU regions unless explicitly requested and contracted.
- Control plane: Redwood Private uses a private control plane model that can be deployed in-customer (customer-controlled) or in a Redwood-hosted private control plane reachable only via PrivateLink/Private Endpoint. In the EU-only configuration we propose PrivateLink into the customer's VPC; no public internet exposure.
- KMS: We support BYOK (customer-managed keys) using a supported KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM). Key operations can be restricted to the EU region. We can also provide Redwood-managed keys with strict partitioning as an alternative.
- Logs/audit: request logs, trace data, and model telemetry can be retained inside the EU region with configurable retention windows; we will provide an exportable audit bundle for your review.

Next steps: Kimberly will attach a short network diagram + KMS flow; Diego will add the operational notes and runbook snippets. I'll attach a short signed Data Residency Declaration (PDF) for your legal team. If you have a SIG spreadsheet, we can pre-fill the relevant rows.

Hi Anna — attaching the technical artefacts we discussed. See the high-level bullets below, and the diagram + KMS flow in the Drive link.

Key technical confirmations (short form):
- Private control plane: For the Medsafe pilot we recommend the PrivateLink model. The control plane endpoints are exposed only as AWS PrivateLink interface endpoints inside the customer's VPC (no public IPs). Control-plane traffic is encrypted TLS 1.3; authentication uses mutual TLS + short-lived mTLS tokens issued by Redwood and optionally rotated by the customer.
- Data plane (inference): All inference nodes and KV/cache live in EC2/GPU instances located in the Frankfurt (eu-central-1) region inside the customer's VPC subnets. KV cache eviction and model artifacts are stored on-region; backups are optionally tenant-scoped and can be configured to remain in-region.
- KMS/BYOK: We support Cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). For EU-only deployments keys can be created and operated in eu-central-1; Redwood never exfiltrates raw key material. We also support HSM import workflows and a sealed-wrap procedure for long-term key custody.
- Audit/logs: Request logs, token traces, and operator audit events are written to an audit bucket (S3) in eu-central-1. We can provide automated S3 lifecycle policies and a signed manifest for your records.
- Cross-region failover: Configuration is opt-in. By default there is no automatic failover to non-EU regions; if you enable a cross-region DR policy we'd provide explicit documentation and require a documented customer opt-in + change control.

Attachments (stubs): private_control_plane_network_diagram.vsdx (Drive link), kms_key_flow.png (Drive preview).

Diego: added two short runbook snippets below for the SIG answers.

—Kimberly

Anna — quick answers inline and next steps: 

> 1) Confirm replication disabled by default
Yes — replication and cross-region copy are disabled by default on all audit buckets and backup artefacts in the EU deployment. Any replication policy requires explicit configuration by the customer and an approved change request; Redwood will not enable replication without documented customer authorization. We will include a signed statement to this effect in the declaration.

> 2) BYOK onboarding and plaintext key handling
We do not persist plaintext key material on Redwood-hosted systems. Supported import paths are envelope-wrapped or HSM import via Cloud KMS import APIs. During the import, plaintext may transiently exist in the customer's environment only; Redwood's onboarding procedure requires customer-supplied wrapped keys or HSM-imported keys. We will include the formal BYOK runbook excerpt in the packet.

> 3) DocuSign for Data Residency Declaration
Attached is a DocuSign powerform link (https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123) and a signed PDF copy of the Data Residency Declaration for your records (redwood_data_residency_declaration_2027.pdf).

We also pre-filled the SIG rows SC-1, SC-7, and PR-4 and uploaded the CSV to the Drive folder (link above).

- We can schedule a 30-min deep-dive with Diego and Rishi this week to walk the runbook and the on-boarding checklist.
